info.description:
The API of an fvoci server.

## Signing in

`login` answers with a `Set-Cookie` header that carries the session: the cookie `__Host-fvoci_session` where the server is reached over HTTPS, `fvoci_session` over plain HTTP. It is `HttpOnly`, so a page's scripts never see it, and a browser sends it by itself. A client that is no browser may send the cookie's value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` instead. A few operations that read a shared board need no session when the request has the board's `readToken`.

## Requests that change something

Every request whose method is not `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` needs the header `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, unless it has a bearer token, and is refused with 403 and the reason `csrf` without it. If it has an `Origin` header, the origin must be the server's own (or one the server was configured to accept); otherwise it is refused with 403 and the reason `foreign_origin`.

A page should make these requests with `fetch` in its default mode, `cors`. The server sends its pages with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and under that policy a browser writes `Origin: null` on a changing request of any other mode (`same-origin`, `no-cors`, or a form the browser posts itself), which is refused as a foreign origin.

## Answers

An operation answers 200 with a body, 201 with what it made, or 204 with no body. Every other status comes with a `Problem`, the problem details of RFC 9457, as `application/problem+json`: `type` names the kind of the problem and is the same for every problem of the kind, `title` is its name, `status` repeats the status and `detail` says what went wrong this time. `type` is `/problems/<name>` under the path the server is served at, the address of a page of text about the kind; `/problems` lists them, and so does `x-problem-types` of the schema `Problem`, as they are on a server at the root of its host (a server under a path has that path before each). `reason` tells apart causes a client must tell apart; a problem with a `reason` has the `type` of that name, written with hyphens, and any other the `type` of its status. `errors` lists what of the request was refused, each by a JSON Pointer into the body (`pointer`), the name of a parameter of the query or the path (`parameter`), or the name of a header (`header`). `limit` is the limit that was exceeded: bytes for a body that was too large (413), a count for too many of something. `instance` is the request, `urn:uuid:` and its `requestId`. A session that is missing or over is 401. What the user may not see is 404, as if it were not there; what they may see but not do is 403. A path that is no operation is 404 too, and a method an operation's path does not have is 405.

A request without a session whose JSON body has more than 64 KiB is 413 before it is 401.

The identifiers of users, workspaces, boards, blocks and categories are UUIDs, written lower-case with hyphens; a client takes every identifier as an opaque string. A `fileId` is no UUID: it is an unguessable name that ends in the file's extension. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

## Lists

Every list comes in an order, and the description of each operation says which. Where it says nothing else, the order is that of creation, oldest first, and by identifier among what was created in the same millisecond.

## Request bodies

A request schema lists the members a request is for. An optional member may be left out or be `null`. A member the schema marks as required is one the request cannot do without; where the server takes a missing one as empty instead of refusing the request, the result is that of the empty value (a login without a password is a failed login). A body with members the schema does not list is mostly not refused for them. The exceptions: `patchUserSettings` and `patchMe` refuse every member they do not know, `createBoard` and `createCategory` refuse an `id`, and `setSharing` refuses a `token`.

Makes the boards of an archive in the workspace, with the user as their admin. The
members the archive names for a board become members of it with the roles they had,
where they are in the workspace. The archive is sent before in parts: open an
upload with `createImportUpload`, send its parts with `putUploadPart`, then name

stays open for it; otherwise the upload ends with the import, whether it succeeds or
not. Another user's upload, or one that has ended, is 404; an upload of a file, or

refused, and the upload is thrown away.

original (the line-based version 1 and the ZIP of version 2) and a ZIP without

`board.jsonl` of more than 64 MiB or a file larger than `maxFileSize` is 413 with

value that does not fit its property's kind is cleared, as a copy does.

many users were left out, not who.
